unit.why: An ethical teaching on shunning honour, quoted from an earlier book, wraps two short anecdotes: the Baal Haflaah's reception in Frankfurt and the Besht being honoured in a town.
unit.boundary_note: part of a continuing ethical discourse on honour that runs from the previous division into the next

stories.start_quote: וסיפרו כשקבלו את הג׳ בעל הפלא״ה
stories.summary_en: When the author of Haflaah was received as rabbi of Frankfurt with great honour, he said he imagined himself being carried on a bier to the cemetery with all the people escorting him.

quotes: שדומה בנפשו שנושאים אותו במטה לבית החיים
tags.why: he deflates the honour by thinking of death
praises a rabbinic authority, the Baal Haflaah of Frankfurt
framed as instruction to flee honour

quotes: כבוד שלא לחמוד כבוד ואדרבה להתרחק מן הכבוד
tags.why: seeking honour is the failing being warned against

stories.summary_en: The Besht, greatly honoured in a town, taught that honour brings heavenly scrutiny of one's deeds, but a wise person turns it into self-examination and repentance.

tags.why: the lesson is about receiving honour humbly
honour as a prompt to repent

quotes: ואמר להם הבעש״ט תדעו כי כשמכבדים

tags.why: mostly a teaching, with only a thin narrative
moral instruction on honour, addressed to 'my dear sons'
the Besht arrives at a place, but only in passing
heavenly judgement is mentioned, not used as a setting
